'''Shang-keng Ma''' (September 24, 1940 – November 24, 1983) was a Chinese theoretical physicist, known for his work on the theory of [[critical phenomena]] and [[random system]]s.<ref name=obit/> He is known as the co-author with [[Bertrand Halperin]] and [[Pierre Hohenberg]] of a 1972 paper that "generalized the renormalization group theory to dynamical critical phenomena."<ref name=obit/> Ma is also known as the co-author with [[Yoseph Imry]] of a 1975 paper<ref name=obit/> and with [[Amnon Aharony]] and Imry of a 1976 paper that established the foundation of the [[random field]] [[Ising model]] (RFIM)<ref>{{cite journal|author=Fytas, N.G.|author2=Martín-Mayor, V.|author3=Picco, M.|author4=Sourlas, N.|year=2018|title=Review of recent developments in the random-field Ising model|journal=Journal of Statistical Physics|volume=172|issue=2|pages=665–672|doi=10.1007/s10955-018-1955-7|arxiv=1711.09597 |bibcode=2018JSP...172..665F |s2cid=115133326 }} [https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.09597 arXiv preprint]</ref>

==Biography==
He transferred in 1959 from the [[National Taiwan University]] to the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. There he graduated in 1962 with a bachelor's degree in science and in 1966 with a Ph.D. His Ph.D. thesis ''Correlations of Photons from a Thermal Source'' was supervised by [[Kenneth M. Watson]]. As a postdoc in 1966, Ma went to the [[University of California, San Diego]] (UCSD) to study with [[Keith Brueckner]]. Ma's outstanding ability earned him a faculty appointment at UCSD in less than a year.<ref name=obit>{{cite journal|doi=10.1063/1.2916178|title=Shang-keng Ma|year=1984|last1=Chen|first1=Joseph C. Y.|last2=Prentis|first2=Jeffrey|last3=Schultz|first3=Sheldon|journal=Physics Today|volume=37|issue=4|pages=102–103|bibcode=1984PhT....37d.102C}}</ref> He was at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] (IAS) from September 1968 to June 1969 and 
in the autumn of 1970.<ref>{{cite web|title=Shang-Keng Ma|website=Institute for Advanced Study (ias.edu)|date=9 December 2019 |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/shang-keng-ma}}</ref> There he worked with Shau-Jin Chang on the infinite-energy limit of [[Feynman diagram]]s<ref name=obit/><ref>{{cite web|title=Shau-Jin Chang|website=Institute for Advanced Study (ias.edu)|date=9 December 2019 |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/shau-jin-chang}}</ref> and with [[Roger Dashen]] on the [[S-matrix]] formulation of [[statistical mechanics]].<ref name=obit/><ref>{{cite web|title=Roger Dashen|website=Institute for Advanced Study (ias.edu)|date=9 December 2019 |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/roger-dashen}}</ref> In 1971 he became a tenured faculty member of the UCSD physics department<ref name=obitOAC>{{cite web|title=Shang-Keng Ma, Physics: San Diego, 1940–1983, Professor|author=Chen, Joseph C. Y.|author2=Schultz, Sheldon|author3=Sham, Lu Jeu|website=Online Archive of California|url=https://oac.cdlib.org/view?docId=hb767nb3z6;NAAN=13030&doc.view=frames&chunk.id=div00074&toc.depth=1&toc.id=&brand=oac4}}</ref> and became a [[Sloan Research Fellow]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Sloan Research Fellows in Physics or Chemistry, 1971|website=Alfred P. Sloan Foundation (sloan.org)|url=https://sloan.org/past-Fellows?page=505}}</ref>

{{blockquote|He visited Cornell University in 1972 where he became involved in development of the renormalization theory of critical phenomena. Gradually, his interest shifted to statistical physics.<ref>{{cite book|author=Wu, Fa Yueh|chapter=Eulogy on Shang-Keng Ma|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=3HtpDQAAQBAJ&pg=PA68|pages=68–69|isbn = 9789812813886|title = Exactly Solved Models: A Journey in Statistical Mechanics : Selected Papers with Commentaries (1963-2008)|year = 2009|publisher = World Scientific}}</ref>}}

{{blockquote|In 1975, with [[Yoseph Imry]], he published the seminal paper on the effect of a random magnetic field on [[Ferromagnetism|ferro-magnetic order]]. Their model has come to be known as the random field Ising model.<ref name=obit/>}}

In 1976 Ma was a visiting scientist at [[Paris-Saclay University]] and published his paper ''Renormalization group by Monte Carlo methods'', which introduced a technique which "has evolved into a powerful technology that is widely used today for the numerical study of critical phenomena."<ref name=obit/>

{{blockquote|In 1981, Ma formulated the "coincidence counting" method for the calculation of entropy from the phase space trajectory. He felt strongly that such a dynamical formulation of entropy was crucial for understanding random and other systems exhibiting metastability.<ref name=obit/>}}

In the two academic years 1977–1978 and 1981–1982 he taught in Taiwan at [[National Tsing Hua University]], where he wrote an advanced text on statistical mechanics in Chinese — the book, published in 1983, "eschews the traditional approach built on the Gibbs ensemble." [[World Scientific]] published an English translation in 1985. In 1986 World Scientific also published a memorial volume in honor of Ma.<ref>{{cite book|editor=Grinstein, Geoffrey|editor2=Mazenko, Gene F.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=WXkGCwAAQBAJ|isbn = 9789814513609|title = Directions in Condensed Matter Physics: Memorial Volume in Honor of Shang-keng Ma|date = August 1986|publisher = World Scientific}} Publications of Shang-Keng Ma: [https://books.google.com/books?id=WXkGCwAAQBAJ&pg=PA249 p. 249] [https://books.google.com/books?id=WXkGCwAAQBAJ&pg=PA250 p. 250] [https://books.google.com/books?id=WXkGCwAAQBAJ&pg=PA251 p. 251] [https://books.google.com/books?id=WXkGCwAAQBAJ&pg=PA252 p. 252]</ref>
